Subject: Model fit follow-up & Redwood-verified benchmarks for ACME

Hi Sarah —

Thanks again for the call today — great to meet you and hear more about ACME's use cases (support deflection + automated summarization). Quick recap and next steps from my side: 

- Goal: production chat + summarization pipeline for support agents (expected steady-state ~50–80 TPS, spiky up to ~120 TPS).
- Primary constraints: 95th pct latency target ~<300ms for short turns, and reliable quality as you scale (monitorable).
- Initial recommendation: run model-fit evals on your prompt set against two model variants we typically recommend: rw-13b-quant (cost-efficient) and rw-70b-8bit (higher quality).

What I can do next:
1) Run a Redwood-hosted eval of your prompt set and return per-prompt quality metrics + latency/TPS numbers (I can do a blind run on your prompts, privacy preserved).
2) Share our Redwood-verified performance profiles + benchmark artifacts for the above models so you can see expected p50/p95/p99 latency and throughput (attached list).
3) Schedule a technical deep-dive with Alex (model performance) and Jordan (infra) to go over integration, canary rollout, and quality regression alerts.

Ask from you: could you share a representative prompt set (few hundred examples is ideal) and any SLOs we should enforce? A Drive link or a short S3 presigned URL works.

If that sounds good, propose: I’ll run the eval on Wed and share results + dashboard links on Thu morning, then we can meet Thu afternoon for a 45m deep-dive.

Thanks — looking forward to it.

Best,
Marissa Cole

Hi Marissa —

Thanks for the recap — that aligns with what we discussed. A few clarifying data points from our side:
- Target steady-state TPS: 50–80 TPS (predominantly short single-turn queries), with short spikes to ~120 TPS.
- Latency SLO: 95th percentile target <= 300ms for the majority of requests.
- Quality: we care most about summary faithfulness and answer relevance; UAT team will provide labeled pass/fail on ~500 prompts.

I uploaded a representative prompt set here: https://drive.google.com/file/d/1a2b3cPromptSetAcme/view (labelled prompt_set_acme_v1.jsonl) — please let me know if the link doesn't work or if you prefer an S3 upload.

Also: can you confirm how Redwood surfaces quality regressions? We need automated alerts when a deployed variant drops below baseline (ideally tied to prompt tests + synthetic evals).

Happy to do Thu afternoon for the deep-dive. 

— Sarah

Hi Sarah —

Thanks — I have the Drive link and will pull the prompt set for the eval. Per your questions, attached is a short Redwood-verified performance summary (PDF) and the prompt set you uploaded. Below are the high-level, verified numbers you asked for (measured on Redwood Dedicated pool, standard inference config for each model):

Model: rw-13b-quant (recommended first pass)
- Throughput (typical): 100–140 TPS (batched, short contexts)
- Latency: p50 40–60 ms, p95 ~150–200 ms, p99 ~260–320 ms
- Notes: very cost-efficient for single-turn short queries; good starting point for ACME if quality checks pass.

Model: rw-70b-8bit (quality-first)
- Throughput (typical): 20–35 TPS
- Latency: p50 110–160 ms, p95 380–480 ms, p99 600+ ms
- Notes: stronger summarization/faithfulness on long-form prompts, higher infra cost.

Operational recommendations:
- Start with rw-13b-quant in a canary serving config (10–20% traffic) and run your labeled prompts to validate quality.
- If we see systematic regressions on summarization metrics, escalate to rw-70b-8bit for that traffic slice.
- Use Redwood Optimize suggestions (auto-batching + prefix caching) — we’ve seen 20–40% unit-cost reductions on similar workloads.
- Quality regression monitoring: Redwood integrates prompt-set based evals + synthetic scoring. We can set a baseline pass-rate and create alerts (Slack/email) when rolling 24h pass-rate drops by >5 percentage points or absolute pass-rate falls below your threshold.

I’ve kicked off an eval run on your prompt_set_acme_v1.jsonl and will upload full per-prompt latency + quality stats to the dashboard here: https://console.redwood.ai/benchmarks/acme-2026 (you’ll see a per-model tab with p50/p95/p99 latency histograms, per-prompt quality scatterplots, and a downloadable CSV).

Attachments included: redwood_benchmarks_acme_20260303.pdf (summary) and prompt_set_acme_v1.jsonl (copied for traceability).

Next steps (proposed):
- Thu 4/Mar 2026 15:00–15:45 PT: technical deep-dive (Alex + Jordan + your infra lead). Confirm if this works.
- After the deep-dive: run a 24–48h canary and produce an ops playbook for rollback/fallback.

If you confirm the time, I’ll send a calendar invite and link to the dashboard export.

Best,
Marissa
